notes: Baseline: the dataset's own system prompt, one call, no extra instructions.

Extractor+solver like c1 (overlaps dominate P0 failures), plus a general soft-preference language (window, avoid_window, before/after_event, adjacent, gap) that the solver maximises, so unseen preference types (spec_A warns they will appear) can still be expressed instead of only prefer_window. Uses /no_think and a smaller max_tokens to keep the cost close to P0's single call.

Same extractor+solver split as c1 (overlaps are ~80% of P0 failures), but the extractor first writes a turn-by-turn ledger before the final spec. Motivated by dev_v2 state-tracking failures: 8 extra_event cases ("revert the calendar to Turn 4"), chit-chat final turns where P0 emitted no calendar (no_json), and events referenced by name without an id ("lock in the 1:1 Martinez at 2:20").

P0 fails mostly on overlaps (48/59 dev_in, 41/62 dev_v2, 19+10 out_of_window on ood_dev): the 8b model cannot pack intervals. c1 turns the single LLM call into a constraint/preference extractor (native chat input) and adds a deterministic tool (release-time/deadline DFS solver) that places events, maximises satisfied preference windows, and relaxes constraints only if the spec is infeasible. On all 36 failures, the solver given true constraints produces valid calendars with 100% preferences met.

Zero-token hypothesis: no LLM at all. The tool takes the last assistant calendar in the chat history (or the Turn-N calendar when the user asks to revert, which caused the 8 dev_v2 extra_event failures), applies the final user turn (add/move/remove, events matched by id or by name), regex-parses every user turn for constraints/durations/preferences, and solves with an exact search that keeps previous placements unless they must move. P0 loses ~0.06 fitness to tokens and its failures are almost all packing errors (overlap/out_of_window) that a solver never makes.

Keeps P0's single LLM call untouched and adds a zero-token deterministic guard (tools/repair.py). If the LLM calendar is broken (no JSON, overlap, out of 10:00-16:00) it regex-parses every user turn for per-event constraints/durations (latest wins, events matched by id or by name) and re-places as few events as possible with an exact min-move search; valid answers pass through unchanged, so it can only fix P0 failures. Motivated by overlap being 48/59 dev_in, 41/62 dev_v2 and 29/43 ood_dev failures, and by extractor-only children (feedback) collapsing to constraint_violated; no_json chit-chat turns reuse the last calendar in the history.

Cheap + aggressive variant: the worker runs with /no_think and a short JSON-only instruction (cuts the ~2.7-3.6k tokens/sample that cost P0 ~0.06 fitness), and the deterministic repair tool does the hard work. Unlike c1 it also repairs answers that violate a constraint regex-parsed from the user turns (violates_before/at were 13 ood_dev failures, e.g. the LLM sacrificing hard constraints to satisfy preferences), and when the last turn states fuzzy preferences it moves only those events into the preference window (general phrase->window table plus clock-time fallback, so unseen phrasings degrade gracefully).

Still zero tokens; fixes the parser/solver of the parent tool. (1) relax() used to drop EVERY constraint once one mis-parsed older constraint made the instance infeasible - that is what the dev_v2/ood violates_at/after failures look like (e.g. "at 10:50am" or "at 1pm" from the final turn ignored), so it now keeps final-turn constraints and frees the fewest, most suspicious older ones first, gated by a cheap feasibility check. (2) Removals from any turn after the base calendar apply (dev_v2 extra_event), names introduced in user turns are learned for name-only references, "toward ..." no longer turns an add into a preference (dev_in missing_event), sentences split on lowercase starts and the latest window phrase wins ("mornings are for deep work, so ... afternoon"; 6 ood soft misses).

Zero tokens. Contains c1's fixes (relax keeps final-turn constraints, earlier-turn removals, user-turn names, preference parsing and weight 2.5) and adds checks for constraints that were parsed wrong: a parsed constraint that a later assistant calendar already breaks is treated as a mis-parse, so it is dropped and the event stays at its historical slot. The dev_v2 failures where an older event's constraint was broken point to infeasibility from wrong old parses. Move phrasing is parsed too: "move X from 11am to 2pm" -> at 2pm (it used to be read as between), and "push back/bring forward by N min" -> an exact start shifted from where the event sits now (no longer read as a duration change).

Zero tokens. Contains all of c1's fixes (relax keeps final-turn constraints instead of dropping all of them, which caused the dev_v2/ood violates_at/after failures; removals from earlier turns; names learned from user turns; sentence splitting and latest-phrase preference windows that fix the 10 ood soft misses; preference weight 2.5 so preferences can move settled events). It also adds a general soft-preference engine aimed at unseen preference types: exact avoid-windows ("keep X out of the morning"), "around T", order (X before/after Y), adjacency (right after/before, back-to-back) and buffer/breathing-room preferences, all scored inside the solver.

Zero tokens. Child 1's history-distrust and parser fixes (dev_v2 constraint violations, missing events) plus more preference credit: 6/8 ood_dev failures were soft misses where a feasible plan met both preferences but needed several settled events moved, so events whose constraint we parsed now move cheaply (w 0.6/1.0 instead of 2.0) and PREF_W is 3.2. Preference parsing is more general for unseen types: explicit-time preferences (before/after/between/around T, the last sized to the event), avoid/"not too early|late", mid-afternoon, before lunch, start of the afternoon.

Zero tokens. Child 2 (history-distrust, parser fixes, stronger and more general preferences) plus robustness to wording the regexes never saw: user text is normalised first ("half past two", "quarter to eleven", "ten thirty am", "three o'clock", "forty-five minutes", "by midday"), and negations are handled ("not after 2pm" -> before, "not until 1pm" -> after). Also drops calendar events whose id no user/system turn ever mentions, since dev_v2 histories can be wrong (v2train-7111 extra_event).

Zero tokens. Stops trusting the assistant history: in dev_v2 most failures put an event back at a historical slot that breaks its stated constraint (after/at/between violations), so the "suspect" rule that dropped any constraint a later calendar broke is off (SUSPECT=False; relax() still drops history-broken constraints first, only when infeasible); events the user added but the history lost are re-added and removals from any turn count (train-94/oodA-3110 missing_event). Fixes parser bugs found by replaying failures: "no later than" read as after, "10:15 or any time after that" read as at, "4-H" read as 4 hours, "Dr. Patel" splitting a preference sentence; name matching prefers live events and phrase overlap; an exact left-shift packing search backs up the capped solver so tight days never drop an event.

Zero tokens. Child 1's negation-aware parser fix ("no later than" was parsed as after), plus SUSPECT=False only. The parent dropped any constraint that a later assistant calendar broke and kept the event at its history slot. dev_v2 histories drift, so failures such as v2train-5100, 2330 and 8450 show old at/after constraints violated on days that are not tight. Those constraints are now enforced, and relax() still falls back to the history slot when the plan is infeasible. The previous a1 children that also removed SUSPECT lost dev_in through unrelated add/remove changes, which are not included here.

Zero tokens. Child 2 (negation-aware parser plus enforcing history-broken constraints) and two general changes. (1) Preference credit: 6 of the 8 ood_dev failures are 0.75 soft misses that need settled events moved. Moving an event within a constraint we parsed is free at grading time, so known events now cost 1.2 to move instead of 2.0, and PREF_W is 3.0. (2) dev_v2 final turns name the event without an id ("lock in the 1:1 Martinez at 2:20 pm"). When strict name matching fails on the last turn, a stem-overlap fallback that normalises "1:1"/"one-on-one" picks the event, but only if it clearly beats the runner-up.

Zero tokens, parser-only fix on the parent. The constraint parser read "no later than 3pm" as AFTER 3pm because "later than" sits in AFTER_PRE. It also read "not start before 2pm" as before, and "no sooner than", "or any time after that" and "sometime past 1pm" as at. Most dev_v2 failures are tight days (355-360 of 360 min) where one inverted constraint makes the plan infeasible, and relax() then drops correct constraints (violates_before/after). Negated cues are now checked first, and more after/before suffixes are recognised. Nothing else changed.

Zero-token parser-only fix. In 13 of the 21 dev_v2 failures an older event drifts outside its window on a tight day, but the solver succeeds on the true constraints, so those constraints were lost or half-parsed. A clause with both a lower and an upper limit ("can't start until 12:30 ... done by 3:30") now becomes a between window instead of keeping only the last cue. "ends/wraps up at T" now reads as a deadline, and spoken or dotted times (2.30pm, half past two, quarter to three, 2 o'clock, 2 in the afternoon, '3pm latest', 'ahead of') are recognised. Name references now try events on the current calendar first, so a removed namesake cannot make the match ambiguous.

Child 2 (parser fixes plus the history-span guard), but with the opposite assumption about noisy history. The parent dropped any parsed constraint that a later assistant calendar violated and pinned that event where history put it. Several dev_v2 failures leave an old event in a spot that violates its true constraint. Here the parsed constraint is kept and enforced, and suspect constraints are only the first thing relax() gives up when the day is infeasible.

Child 1's parser fixes, plus a general guard in the solver against constraints we fail to parse. Most dev_v2 violations are old events with no parsed constraint that get moved off their window when the final turn forces a reshuffle on a full day. Every calendar since an event was last discussed honoured its real constraint, so the span of those placements lies inside its true window. That span is now a strong soft penalty (3.0, above a preference's 2.5) for non-final, unconstrained events, and the solver prefers moving events whose window it actually knows.

Child 2, plus two robustness changes in the solver. (1) The parent's own premise is that later calendars honour earlier requests. So a duration parsed before the base calendar now yields to that calendar's duration, and only later durations (normally the final turn's) override it; this targets the wrong_duration failures (ood 2493, v2 6493). (2) Feasibility uses an exact subset DP (earliest-finish over left-packed orders) instead of a 60k-node-capped DFS. The same DP backs up solve() when the DFS finds nothing. On full 355-360 min days a capped search can wrongly report infeasible, and relax() then drops correct constraints or returns the stale base calendar, as in v2 2231 (the final event left unmoved).

Child 1's fixes for unlinked no-id adds and names, plus preference-first move costs. Five of the six ood_dev soft misses (1871, 195, 801, 1045, 3513) had both preferences satisfiable, but every settled event cost 2.0 to move against 2.5 per missed preference. Moving costs nothing in grading; it only hedges against constraints we failed to read. So an event whose request we parsed now costs 0.6, and never-parsed events keep 2.0. For unseen preference types, more phrase families are recognised (before/after lunch, mid-afternoon, as early/late as possible, first half...), and time-anchored wishes ("ideally before 2pm", "between 1 and 3 would be great") become windows through the constraint parser.

Zero tokens. 11 of the 12 dev_v2 failures name the event without an id, and v2 adds lack ids too, so "add X for 50 min, after 2pm" matched no known event and its constraint was dropped. Tight days then moved those events off their window (violates_after/at/between). Synthetic no-id replays of all 12 failures fail on the parent and pass here. A clause with no id and no name match is now held and attached to the event that first appears in the next assistant calendar. A final-turn add with no id gets the next free id. Name matching tries the current calendar first and rewards in-order word pairs. Durations and times are read with event names blanked out ("4-H Club" used to parse as 240 min). Sentence splitting no longer breaks on "Dr.", which had lost a preference in oodA-1771.

Child 1's name/duration/removal fixes, plus solver robustness. (1) A final-turn reference that ties on name score now goes to the strict leader on the current calendar instead of being dropped; v2 2231/8683/5429/7574 left the final "at T" event unmoved. (2) relax() tries dropping pairs of older constraints before dropping all of them, for v2 5429's mass violations. (3) PREF_W rises from 2.5 to 4.0, since moves are free in grading, so preferences can buy more moves; ood 1045 and 3110 missed satisfiable lunchtime and end-of-day windows on fully packed days.

Zero-token fix for event-name resolution, which causes most dev_v2 failures. Name matching now uses stemmed tokens: "Outcome Analysis" matches "Analyzing Intervention Outcomes" (v2 4990, where the final "at 1:50pm" was dropped). An id-less request that quotes an existing title now refers to that event and is not treated as a new one; in v2 7316, "slot the Stakeholder Briefing: New Event..." had created an extra Event 4. Durations now also parse from number words and compounds ("forty-five minutes", "an hour and 15 minutes"), which may explain the missing events in train-94 and v2 7041. More removal phrasings are recognised ("no longer need", "call off", "take X off"), aimed at the extra event in v2 7111.

Child 1's name/duration/removal fixes, plus a general preference representation for soft types not yet seen. The parent only models one-event time windows. The solver now also scores relations between events: order ("X before Y"), back-to-back or "right after", buffer/gap between events or around one event, and global "keep lunch/12-1 free" avoid-windows applied to every event. Each unmet relation costs PREF_W, the same as a window. These are parsed only from soft-cued sentences with no clock time. Motivation: future evaluation adds unseen preference types, and ood_dev is already 0.97 soft on windows.

Child 1's naming fix, plus constraints that outrank a wrong history. v2 histories contain assistant calendars that break earlier constraints (v2 8450 event 3 at 11:40 despite 'after 11:45am'; v2 5429 base breaks 3 constraints). The parent's 'suspect' rule dropped any constraint a later calendar ignored. That rule now applies only to ambiguous parses; a constraint stated with an explicit event id and a single clock time (or one range) is kept hard. Removal cues are also broadened ('no longer need', 'call off', 'take X off', 'scratch'), aimed at the extra event in v2 7111.

Child 1's naming fix, plus fully distrusting the history (a stronger version of child 2's hypothesis). The 'suspect' rule is removed: every parsed constraint stays hard, and relax() still frees the events whose base breaks their constraint first if the set is infeasible (v2 8450, 5429). A removal the history's assistant ignored also still applies, unless the event is mentioned again later; reverts are unchanged. Removal cues are broadened. Target: v2 7111, where an event the user dropped stayed on the calendar.

Zero-token naming fix. A user phrase like "add a 45-minute slot for X (event id: 7)" set the stored name to "45-minute slot", so later title references (v2 7574, 2231, 8683, 5429) matched nothing. Now calendar titles always override user-derived names. Two final-turn-only fallbacks are added: stemmed matching (v2 4990), and treating an id-less "slot the <existing title> ..." as a reference rather than a new event (v2 7316). Last generation's global stemming, number-word and removal changes, which cost dev_in, are left out.

Zero tokens, two narrow history fixes. (1) Restore lost events: an event the user explicitly added (known duration, never removed) but absent from the base calendar is put back, if no assistant calendar ever contained it or no later user turn contains any removal-like word. Targets missing_event in train-94 (75-min event 5 lost) and v2 7041 (event 6 lost). (2) In the final turn, an id-less "slot <title>" request whose text contains an existing event's full title verbatim refers to that event and does not create a new one (v2 7316's extra "Event 4"). Name matching is otherwise untouched.

The solver is unchanged, but final-turn name resolution gets a tiny LLM fallback. A probe tool runs the parent's parser. Only when a final-turn clause has a time, duration, shift, removal or preference and matches no event by id or by the name-overlap heuristic does it emit the current id:title list and the clause. qwen3-8b then picks the id; otherwise the prompt is about 40 tokens and the reply is "-". The parent silently drops these clauses, which explains most dev_v2 failures (2231, 8683, 7574, 4990, 5429: the final "at T" event is left unmoved). Earlier zero-token fixes (global stemming, title overrides) cost dev_in, so here behaviour changes only where the parent did nothing.

Combines child 1 (LLM fallback only for final-turn clauses the parser cannot tie to an event: v2 2231/8683/7574/4990/5429) with child 2 (restore events the history lost: train-94, v2 7041; verbatim-title reference instead of a new event: v2 7316). PREF_W also rises from 2.5 to 4.0, because moves are free in grading. In ood 1045 and 3110, satisfiable lunchtime and end-of-day windows were missed because moving 4+ settled events cost more than the preference was worth.

Conservative fix: only the name-resolution changes; the parent's trust in history is unchanged. Tokens compare 5-letter stems ('Outcome Analysis' -> 'Analyzing Intervention Outcomes', v2 4990). resolve() can pick an event outside the latest calendar when it scores clearly higher (v2 7574 moved the wrong event to 10:45). An 'add' clause that quotes at least 60% of an existing title is treated as a reference, not a new event (v2 7316's 'New' in the title triggered ADD_RE and created 'Event 4'). This tests whether the v2 losses are reference errors rather than distrust of history.

Middle ground between c1 and c2: includes all of c1 (stemmed or off-calendar name resolution, the add-vs-reference guard, keeping events that were added by id but lost from a later calendar). It keeps the parent's 'suspect' rule only for constraints attached by fuzzy name matching. A constraint read from a clause that names the event by id is always kept, even if a later assistant calendar breaks it (train-3640, v2 8450/5429). Hypothesis: the suspect rule protected against fuzzy-reference misreads, while id-explicit constraints are reliable and the history calendars are the noisy part.

Distrust the chat history and trust the user's words. (1) Removed the 'suspect' rule that dropped a parsed constraint whenever a later assistant calendar broke it. Assistant calendars in dev_in and dev_v2 are sometimes wrong (train-3640 at 11:15, v2 8450/5429 after/before limits left broken), and relax() still drops such constraints first if the day is infeasible. (2) An event the user added by id and never removed or reverted is kept even when a later calendar lost it (train-94 missing event 5). (3) Name resolution compares 5-letter stems and can choose an event that is not on the current calendar when it fits the words clearly better (v2 4990 'Outcome Analysis', 7574). An 'add' turn that quotes most of an existing title re-times that event instead of creating a new one (v2 7316 made a phantom 'Event 4').

Minimal name fix: every assistant/system calendar now overwrites the stored event name with its full title (the parent used setdefault, so a name lifted from user text stuck forever - e.g. only the inner quote "Molecular Structures in Sculpture" for v2 7574, making 'Science-Art Workshop ... senior learners' resolve to event 3). Name-resolution failures explain most dev_v2 losses (2231, 8450, 8683, 5429, 4990, 7574: the final-turn 'at' target was the wrong or no event even though the final-calendar names match uniquely). Still zero LLM tokens.

Calendar titles become canonical names, but the user's own wording is kept as an alias unioned into the matching tokens (alternative to child 1's plain override). Constraints that a later assistant calendar broke ('suspect') are no longer discarded; they become soft windows (weight 2.5 vs move cost 0.6), so the solver restores them when cheap - train-3640 (event 0 'at 11:15' slipped to 10:45 by an earlier reply, then kept there) is reproduced by the parent and fixed here. Zero LLM tokens.

Child 1's calendar-title name fix plus membership rebuilt from the user's own add/remove history: an event the user added by explicit id with a duration is restored even if a later assistant reply dropped it (train-94 lost event 5, v2 7041 lost event 6), and a removal stays applied even if a later assistant reply kept the event (v2 7111 extra 'Post-Event Debrief'). Reverts keep the parent's behaviour. Zero LLM tokens.

Same alias-vs-title dispute rule as c1, applied to every user turn rather than only the final one. A disagreement goes to the event whose alias plus title explains more of the user's words. Names are never overwritten, so pending/add detection and scrubbing still use the parent's wording. This tests whether earlier-turn constraints also attach to the wrong event when the user paraphrases a calendar title (the dev_v2 failures hint at stale aliases). The parent's suspect/membership logic is unchanged, so a1_c3's soft-suspect regression is not repeated. Zero LLM tokens.

Final-turn-only name fix, keeping the parent's first-seen names everywhere else. A separate titles map holds the latest calendar title of each event. The final turn's reference is also matched against the current titles. When that disagrees with the parent's alias match, or the alias match finds nothing, the event whose alias plus title accounts for more of the user's words wins. Evidence: every dev_v2 'at' loss (2231, 8450, 8683, 5429, 7574, 4990) resolves correctly against the full titles, and the 7574 inner-quote alias pulls the move onto event 3. The a1 override children lost dev_in because they replaced names in every turn; this child leaves earlier turns alone. Zero LLM tokens.

c1's final-turn title-vs-alias resolution, but the 8B worker arbitrates genuine disputes. The probe tool (phase 1) emits a tiny two-option question only when the alias match and the current-title match name different events; otherwise it emits "none". The planner (phase 2) uses the pick only if it is one of the two candidates, else it falls back to the word-coverage rule. This targets the dev_v2 name-reference losses (7574 etc.) with an LLM's paraphrase understanding, at roughly 50-150 prompt tokens per sample.

Tightened REMOVE_RE: 'clear' now counts as a removal only as a verb with an object ('clear the X'), and 'drop by/in' no longer counts. Evidence: 3 of the 8 hard failures (train-2965, v2train-4861, train-1454) are small-talk final turns ('a clear risk matrix', 'clear window to focus', 'that clear slot after 10:30'), which deleted the event the sentence named, giving [] or a missing event. This is a minimal one-regex fix; nothing else changed. Zero LLM tokens.

Has c1's 'clear' removal fix. Also, in the final turn only, an id-less paragraph whose sentences name two or more different events is split into one group per event (sentences that name no event stay with the one before), so a time goes to the event its own sentence names. Evidence: v2train-4994 ('Workshop is set to wrap by 11:30. The client pitch ... ') gave 'before 11:30' to the pitch, whose title matched more words, and pushed the workshop past 11:30. Zero LLM tokens.

Has c1's 'clear' removal fix. Also, outside reverts, an event that was on an earlier calendar, or that the user added by id with a duration, but is missing from the latest calendar is put back unless some turn asked to remove it. Evidence: train-94 (event 5) and v2train-7041 (event 6) fail with missing_event, while the gold still expects those events, so trusting the latest calendar's event set loses them. Zero LLM tokens.

Parse fix only. In a clause with no event id, a time now belongs to the event named in the sentence that holds the time, not to whichever event the whole clause matches best. Evidence: v2train-4994's small-talk final turn says "the Brand Narrative Workshop is set to wrap by 11:30" and then talks at length about the Client Pitch, so the parent gave "before 11:30" to the pitch and pushed the workshop to 11:30. I reproduced that exact wrong answer and confirmed the fix on a synthetic copy. Still zero LLM tokens.

c1's sentence-level time attribution, plus a solver hedge for constraints the parser missed. Every calendar since an event's last request honoured that request, so [earliest start, latest end] across those calendars is a safe span. Leaving it costs HIST_W=0.5, doubled when the event never moved and its start looks pinned (a typed time, or a start that neither opens the day nor follows another event). Evidence: train-3640 (an "at 11:15" event moved to 10:45; I reproduced the parent's exact output and this fixes it) and v2train-8450 (an "after 11:45" event repacked to 11:40).

c2 plus two changes. (1) An event the user added with an explicit id and never removed is put back even when the last assistant calendar dropped it (train-94 lost a 75-min event 5 this way). (2) Moves are cheaper inside the safe history span and dearer outside it (SAFE_W 0.3, UNK_W 0.8, HIST_W 1.0), so a soft preference can reshuffle several events safely; motivated by oodA-1045, where the lunchtime preference went unmet although a valid layout existed.

Same word-to-digit normalizer as c1, plus two hedges in the history solver. (1) Move-cost tie-break: an event whose time limit was parsed costs 0.5 to move (it stays legal inside its window), while an event read as unconstrained costs 0.75 (it may hide a limit we missed). In train-3640 both repairs cost 1.1, and the parent moved the pinned 11:15 event instead of the 'before 4pm' one. (2) An event the user asked for since the base calendar but whose length could not be read gets 30 min instead of being dropped (dev_in missing_event).

Adds a normalize() pass that rewrites user text written out in words into digits before any parsing: word numbers before units ("seventy-five minutes"), compound lengths ("an hour and a quarter", "1 hour 15 minutes"), clock phrases ("quarter past eleven", "quarter to twelve", "half past one", "ten o'clock", "eleven fifteen am", "11.15am") and "turn two". Evidence: all 3 parent failures involve quarter-hour values (missing 75-min event 5, lost 'at 11:15' on train-3640, 'after 11:45' broken on v2train-8450); the parent drops an event added 'for ninety minutes' and ignores 'quarter past eleven' on synthetic copies, and this child fixes both. Still zero LLM tokens.

Same word-to-digit normalizer and 30-min default length for unreadable durations as c2. Instead of c2's flat weights, the move cost of an event read as unconstrained grows with how many recent history calendars kept it at the same start (0.6 + 0.25 per extra stable calendar, up to 1.35), since a pinned slot usually means a limit we failed to parse. Evidence: train-3640 moved event 0 off its long-held 11:15 'at' slot; on a synthetic copy this child keeps it in place.

History-envelope hedge in the solver. Every history calendar honours the constraints in force when it was written, so for an event we read as unconstrained, the span of its past placements (earliest start to latest end) is a window its real constraint always allows. Leaving that span now costs ENV_W=0.4, plus PIN_W=0.3 more move cost when the event sits exactly at a clock time the user typed. Evidence: train-3640 moved event 0 off its long-held 11:15 slot rather than the 'before 4pm' event 2, and v2train-8450 slid event 3 to 11:40, below every earlier placement (its real limit was 'after 11:45'). I reproduced 3640 on a synthetic copy, and this child fixes it. Zero tokens.

Combines c1 and c2: the history-envelope hedge for events read as unconstrained (train-3640 kept event 0 at its long-held 11:15 slot, v2train-8450 kept event 3 at or after its earliest past start) plus the general relational and avoid preference mechanism (order, adjacency, gap, true no-overlap windows, a wish without an id goes to the turn's event). ENV_W=0.4 is set below PREF_W minus the cost of moving a never-parsed event, so the envelope breaks ties without blocking a move a preference asks for. This tests whether the two gains add up. Zero tokens.

General preference mechanism for preference types not seen yet (this is not aimed at the current 3 failures). Adds relational soft preferences scored over the whole schedule: order (X before or after another event), adjacency (right after, back-to-back), and gap or buffer between events or around one event. "Avoid" windows are now true no-overlap windows; the parent used the complementary half-day, which can overlap lunch. A wish in a paragraph with no event id now applies to the event this turn introduced, and the add request in a wish paragraph is still applied. Evidence: on synthetic copies, "a 15 minute buffer between it and the Design Sync" made the parent change the Design Sync to 15 minutes (a hard failure), and the parent ignored order, avoid and adjacency wishes. Paragraphs that contain a clock time are never taken as preferences. Zero tokens.

Bug fix only. A later clause on a known event that gives a length and happens to contain an add word ("make the Bingo Call (event id: 0) 30 minutes for the new volunteers") reset that event's parsed time limit to None. Now only a fresh add, or a re-add after removal, clears it. Evidence: on a synthetic copy of train-3640 the parent output was identical to the failing answer (event 0 moved off its 'at 11:15' slot) and this child fixes it. v2train-8450 ('after 11:45' lost on event 3) may fit the same pattern. Zero tokens.

c1's constraint-preservation fix, plus parsing fixes for lost events. (1) User text is normalized first: Unicode dashes and spaces become ASCII, and written-out or compound lengths become minutes ("seventy-five minutes", "1 hour 15 minutes" was read as 60, "an hour and a quarter", "1½ hours"). (2) A clause with several ids was skipped entirely, which drops a new event added as "add A (event id: 5) for 75 minutes, right after B (event id: 0)". It is now cut at the last comma or 'and' between id mentions, and each piece goes to its own id. Evidence: train-94 is missing its 75-min event 5. On synthetic copies the parent drops the event for the multi-id and U+2010-dash phrasings, and gives it 60 min for "1 hour 15 minutes". Zero tokens.

c1's constraint-preservation fix (train-3640, v2train-8450) plus the Unicode and compound-length normalizer from c2, but without the multi-id splitting, to keep the risk apart. Adds a general preference change for unseen preference types: a negated wish ("not around lunchtime", "avoid the morning") is now a real no-overlap window scored in the solver, where the parent used the complementary half-day as a stand-in. Zero tokens.
